== History ==
The deity {{ill|Kamuyaimimi|fr|Kamuyaimimi|ja|神八井耳命|ko|카무야이미미노미코토|simple|Kamuyaimimi|zh|神八井耳命|qid=Q11588756}} is a son of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ar|الإمبراطور جينمو|arz|الامبراطور جينمو|as|জিম্মু|az|Cimmu|bcl|Emperador Jimmu|be|Імператар Дзіму|ca|Jinmu|cdo|Sìng-ū Tiĕng-huòng|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر جینمو|cs|Džimmu|de|Jimmu|el|Αυτοκράτορας Τζίμου|eo|Imperiestro Jinmu|es|Jinmu Tennō|et|Jimmu|eu|Jimmu enperadorea|fa|امپراتور جینمو|fi|Jinmu|fr|Jinmu|hak|Sṳ̀n-vú Thiên-fòng|he|ג'ימו, קיסר יפן|hi|सम्राट जिममु|hr|Jinmu|hu|Dzsinmu japán császár|id|Jimmu|it|Jinmu|ja|神武天皇|jv|Jimmu Tenno|ka|ძიმუ|ko|진무 천황|kw|Emperour Jimmu|la|Jimmu|lt|Imperatorius Džinmu|lv|Džimmu|mn|Эзэн Хаан Жиммү|mr|जिम्मू|ms|Maharaja Jimmu|my|ဂျင်းမူ ဧကရာဇ်|nl|Jimmu|no|Jimmu|pl|Jimmu|pt|Jimmu|ru|Император Дзимму|sh|Car Jimmu|simple|Emperor Jimmu|sl|Cesar Džinmu|sr|Џинму|sv|Jimmu|th|จักรพรรดิจิมมุ|tl|Emperador Jimmu|tr|Jimmu|uk|Імператор Дзімму|uz|Jimmu|vi|Thiên hoàng Jimmu|war|Emperador Jimmu|wuu|神武天皇|zh|神武天皇|zh_classical|神武天皇|zh_min_nan|Sîn-bú Thian-hông|zh_yue|神武天皇|qid=Q200188}}. The shrine name is connected with traditions about descendants of this line and the "Shimada" surname.<ref>''Shinsen Shojiroku''.</ref>

From the late Heian period onward, ties with {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ca|Gran santuari de Kasuga|co|Grandi Santuariu Kasuga|cs|Svatyně Kasuga|de|Kasuga-Taisha|es|Kasuga-taisha|eu|Kasuga-taisha|fa|کاسوگا-تایشا|fi|Kasuga-taisha|fr|Kasuga-taisha|he|מקדש קאסוגה|id|Kuil Agung Kasuga|it|Santuario Kasuga|ja|春日大社|ka|კასუგა-ტაისია|ko|가스가타이샤|la|Kasuga-taisha|pl|Kasuga Taisha|pt|Kasuga-taisha|ru|Касуга тайся|sh|Kasuga-taisha|simple|Kasuga Taisha|sl|Svetišče Kasuga|th|ศาลเจ้าคาซูงะ|tok|tomo sewi suli Kasuka|tr|Kasuga-taisha|uk|Касуга тайся|zh|春日大社|qid=Q714559}} deepened. Together with other shikinaisha, it was invited to Kasuga's sacred mountain area and worshiped as one of four deities at Kasuga's Kii Shrine. Later records place the shrine at several locations around Yashima. In 1886, when the area of present Yashima Mausoleum was developed as Prince Sawara's mausoleum, the shrine and Sudo Tenno Shrine were moved and merged at the current site.

== Enshrined deities ==
* Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto
* Sudo Tenno ({{ill|Prince Sawara|fa|شاهزاده ساوارا|fr|Sawara (prince)|ja|早良親王|ko|사와라 친왕|sh|Princ Sawara|tr|Prens Sawara|zh|早良親王|qid=Q1079634}})

== Precinct shrines ==
* Amaterasu Shrine - {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu Omikami}}
* Kasuga Shrine - {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|fr|Ama-no-Koyane-no-mikoto|it|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋命|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯀꯣꯌꯅꯦ|pt|Ame-no-Koyane|ru|Амэ-но коянэ-но микото|simple|Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天兒屋命|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}} and Wa-no-shita Okami
* Small shrine enshrining Konjin

== Main sanctuary ==
The honden is an old-style Kasuga-zukuri building (2.53 m x 1.92 m) with decorative metal fittings and a large porch. It is regarded as a transferred former Kasuga building ("Kasuga-utsushi"), later moved again at the time of merger in 1886. Different theories exist on the precise transfer date and original hall. It was designated a Nara City cultural property on March 1, 1982.

== Stone lanterns ==
Because of the merger with Sudo Tenno Shrine, many lanterns bear inscriptions such as "Sudo Tenno" and "Yashima Tenno," including examples dated 1640, 1710, and 1754.
